flags.reason: This paper is a cochlear/auditory physiology study, not a transcranial brain stimulation study; ultrasound is delivered to the middle/inner ear (bone conduction or ossicle stimulation) rather than to the brain. Target and exposure fields were mapped onto the closest available schema categories (cochlea).
Two different tone-burst durations were used across sub-experiments (6 ms for ABR, 240 ms for cochlear microphonic recordings) at the same frequencies; both are listed rather than choosing one.

Stimulus intensities are reported only in dB (relative to a defined standard pressure of 2 mPa for bone/ossicle conduction, or an unspecified reference for air conduction); converting dB to kPa requires an assumed reference and was not attempted.
Stimulus intensities are reported only in dB (relative to a defined standard pressure of 2 mPa for bone/ossicle conduction); converting dB to kPa requires an assumed reference and was not attempted.

Of the 190 total guinea pigs, 128 were used for ABR/CM experiments and 62 for OCT imaging/vibration recording; not all animals were necessarily exposed to frequencies exceeding the hearing range (e.g., some air-conduction-only calibration).

readout_other: Auditory brainstem response (ABR); cochlear microphonic potential (CM) local field potential recorded via a silver electrode near the round window; optical coherence tomography (OCT) vibrometry of the organ of Corti
direction_notes: Ultrasound above the guinea pig hearing range, delivered by bone conduction or by direct stimulation of the malleus-incus complex (ossicle stimulation), elicited auditory brainstem responses and cochlear microphonic potentials, and evoked nanoscale vibrations of the organ of Corti in the cochlear hook region at both the fundamental stimulus frequency and its 2nd/3rd harmonics.

exposures.label: Bone-conducted ultrasonic stimulation of the cochlea

device.model: Piezoelectric actuator (PC4QM, Thorlabs) with ceramic rod, driven by function generator (WF1948, NF Corporation)

timing.protocol_description: For ABR, 6 ms tone bursts with 0.5 ms rising and falling phases were generated; applied frequencies included 10, 16, 22, 30, 40, 80, 103, 127, 152, 176, 201, and 251 kHz in bone-conducted stimulation. For CM recordings, 240 ms tone bursts of 80, 103, 127, 152, 176, 201, and 251 kHz with 20 ms rising and falling phases were used; stimulus levels were swept from 70 to 100 dB (calibrated re: a standard pressure of 2 mPa for bone conduction).

exposures.label: Direct ossicle (malleus-incus complex) ultrasonic stimulation of the cochlea

device.model: Piezoelectric actuator (PC4QM, Thorlabs) with tapered stainless rod, driven by function generator (WF1948, NF Corporation)

timing.protocol_description: For ABR, 6 ms tone bursts with 0.5 ms rising and falling phases were generated; applied frequencies included 10, 16, 22, 30, 40, 80, 103, 127, 152, 176, 201, and 251 kHz in ossicle stimulation. For CM recordings, 240 ms tone bursts of 80, 103, 127, 152, 176, 201, and 251 kHz with 20 ms rising and falling phases were used; stimulus levels were swept from 70 to 100 dB (calibrated re: a standard pressure of 2 mPa for ossicle stimulation).
